source.title: Scaling Laws for Mixture Pretraining Under Data Constraints
source.authors: Anastasiia Sedova; Skyler Seto; Natalie Schluter; Pierre Ablin

record.file_problem: None noted; the text appears complete. The paper gives inconsistent largest-model sizes in different sections (805M, 936M, and 939M).
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates a repetition-aware loss scaling law for data-constrained mixtures. Its results show that repetition can cause held-out target loss to rise, and that extrapolation and optimal-mixture predictions are setup-dependent and imperfect. This refines the scope of scaling-law claims rather than reproducing the original laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as prior work, but those cited results are not rows. Rows focus on the paper's own loss-law fit comparisons, held-out size extrapolation, optimal-repetition finding, and downstream benchmark averages.
record.test_reason: The study fits and extrapolates a Chinchilla-style power law in repetition-discounted effective data to target-domain held-out loss. It covers more than 2,000 data-constrained mixture runs (101M–~900M parameters). It shows loss bending upward under heavy repetition, where a repetition-agnostic power law in raw tokens extrapolates worse. This restates scaling-law form for the repeated-data regime (V5, V7), tests small-gap extrapolation (V2) and reports downstream accuracy versus scale (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that repeated target tokens give diminishing returns and that generic data lets mixtures tolerate 15–20× repetition. Their repetition-aware law predicts target loss and optimal mixtures better than repetition- or domain-agnostic baselines. They concede size extrapolation is imperfect (wasted tokens), quality filtering is harder to predict, and behaviour beyond ~900M parameters is untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses target-domain held-out loss in mixed, data-constrained pretraining and a repetition-aware effective-data law with saturation and a target-weight penalty; it is not a reproduction of Kaplan or Hoffmann's original scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on target-data size, target weight/repetition, model scale, domain or language, quality-filter band, and the chosen scaling-law formulation. The paper says alternative observation weights preserve the formula ranking, and notes that training-hyperparameter interactions and architecture transfer remain untested.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal target repetition grows with training budget to 15–20 (bilingual) and ~30 (three-domain, small pools). It falls with pool size and model size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In data-constrained mixtures, the loss-minimising repetition of scarce target data grows with compute and exceeds single-source limits; this is not the N/D split of V3.

record.problems: The experiments use one GPT-2-style architecture family and models roughly 100M–900M parameters; larger-scale extrapolation remains unverified. Training hyperparameters were not jointly tuned with mixture and repetition. Size-extrapolation wasted-token results are imperfect, and quality filtering is harder to predict. No statistical uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported scaling-law metrics.
record.rows_left_out: The individual benchmark scores underlying the reported average accuracies in Tables 11–12 are not separately listed; the reported Avg column is retained for each model, language, and target-pool condition. Numerous separate language/domain loss-curve plots and quality-filter conditions in Appendix Figures 11–28 are not catalogued individually; the directly relevant aggregate statements and selected reported results are included. Results cited from earlier studies are excluded.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss in N, D or C in the non-bottlenecked regime. Unlimited-data runs (Fig. 27–28) are not fitted.
Extrapolation over orders of magnitude. Gaps tested are under 2× in model size and 2× in training steps.
No compute-optimal N vs D allocation.
Single depth-scaled GPT-2 family; shape not varied at fixed N.
Other modalities, fine-tuning and transfer. Only the repeated-data, text-mixture regime is tested.
No fitted quantitative mapping from loss or scale to downstream accuracy.
Parameter-counting conventions and training schedule (constant LR only) not varied. Exponent values across setups are not reported.

missing.what: Size-extrapolation wasted-token fractions: Lsize 58% German, 24% Maths; ≥94% for all formulas on French/Swahili.
Test wR² of each formula under four observation-weighting schemes. Lfix ranges 0.78–0.96 by weighting, while the ranking is stable.
Optimal-mixture log-error per formula (Lfix avg 0.19; quality 0.47).
Best achievable target loss vs unique target data and model size, described as remarkably regular (figure only, no fit). Unlimited-data baseline keeps improving while constrained pools plateau.

record.verdict_notes: Reader's V7 'challenges' label was inverted: V7 asserts that curves bend and that results depend on fitting choices, and these results show exactly that, so it is now 'supports'. F1–F4 relinked from V7 to V5 (repeated-data regime). Largest-model size is inconsistent across sections (805M/936M/939M). No uncertainty estimates are reported. Constant learning-rate schedule throughout.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test ordinary held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute in the regime where the other quantities are not bottlenecks.
Tests the paper's repetition-aware mixture law, not the original power laws; the held-out size gaps are substantially less than orders of magnitude.
Does not jointly find compute-optimal parameter count and token count or fit their growth as powers of compute. It studies target mixture weights and repetition instead.
Uses one GPT-2-style decoder-only architecture family and does not compare architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Experiments remain text pretraining mixtures. It does not test image/video modalities, fine-tuning, or transfer, nor whether the original power-law form holds across those regimes.
Reports downstream benchmark accuracy at selected best-target-loss checkpoints, but does not test a quantitative mapping from pretraining loss to downstream performance.

Tests repetition-aware versus alternative formula choices and reports overfitting in constrained mixtures. It does not systematically vary parameter-count conventions or training schedules to estimate their effects on exponents.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: German downstream benchmark averages at best-target-loss checkpoints

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: English downstream benchmark averages at best-target-loss checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: English averages tend to fall as the German target pool grows, while larger models have higher averages; downstream changes therefore depend on domain allocation and are not a simple uniform improvement with scale or target-loss optimization (D21–D40).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Data-constrained mixtures and alternative loss-law formulations
reader_labels.reason: Target loss can rise after repetition, and repetition-aware and repetition-agnostic formulas have different held-out fit performance across datasets, indicating that a single unqualified loss curve/formulation is insufficient in this setting (O1, O2, F1–F8, Q1).
